My father, Jim Brown, was not just a football player. He was one of the most dominant athletes to ever live and one of the greatest men of impact this world has seen. With the Cleveland Browns, he played 9 seasons, made 9 straight Pro Bowls, earned repeated All-NFL honors, brought the Browns their only NFL championship, and retired with 12,312 rushing yards, 106 rushing touchdowns, and a record 104.3 rushing yards per game. He did not just play the game. He changed the standard of greatness. My father is in the Pro Football Hall of Fame, College Football Hall of Fame, and the National Lacrosse Hall of Fame. He excelled in the decathlon, and was invited to the Olympics and to play in the NBA. He did not just dominate one sport—he left his mark across multiple levels of sports legacy. My father was also a builder beyond sports and entertainment. He founded the Black Economic Union, to create economic opportunities for Black-owned businesses. He also founded Amer-I-Can to teach life-management skills that could help break cycles of gang violence, incarceration, and poverty. He helped bring rival gang leaders from the Crips and Bloods together in our home in Los Angeles as part of a peace treaty. My father has always been about real social change. What many people don’t know about my father is that he was also a music manager. He founded and managed The Friends of Distinction and Earth, Wind & Fire. He was a tour manager for the first Temptations national tour and helped Malcolm X’s family in their time of need after he was no longer in the Nation. My father’s greatness did not stop on the football field. When I look back, I realize I would not want it any other way. His greatest legendary impact was his creation of me and how he raised me with a Legendary Mindset. My dad was my provider, my leader, and the man in my life who fulfilled my needs. My dad was always there for me. Especially when I called him, he would always pick up the phone, and this was before cell phones. Face to face, we would talk for hours about the same thing— how to change the world. That’s what he instilled in me. ABOUT MY FATHER 3 February 17, 1936 - May 18, 2023
